audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics that change decisions are missing. Primordial Burst deals damage 'increasing based on the target's missing health' — nowhere on the page, and it inverts the usual advice: trading yourself low does not just risk the combo, it makes the combo bigger. And Phenomenal Evil stacks from striking an enemy CHAMPION with a spell or scoring a takedown, not only from Baleful Strike farm kills — so every poke he lands on you is permanent AP. The page treats stack denial as purely a wave-management problem.
audit.why: enemyKit R text: 'dealing a large amount of magic damage, increasing based on the target's missing health.' enemyKit P text: 'Striking an enemy Champion with a spell or scoring a takedown grants Veigar permanently increased Ability Power.'
audit.corrected: tradeBad, breakdown.early, breakdown.feeding and report[5].t now carry both facts.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contains no digit — defect-catalogue item 3 — despite Event Horizon's 20s rank-1 cooldown being the single most exploitable number in the matchup. Separately dosFull[2].d calls it 'the fifteen-second invitation', which is wrong at every rank the lane phase is played at: it is 20s at rank 1 and only reaches 14s at rank 5.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt with the real numbers, and dosFull[2].d now says 20 seconds.

notes: CHART: content win[0..6] already matches packet.levelChart (Neeko on all seven), so only the four stale full-layer sides moved and no no-op win[N] edits were proposed. None of the four rows changed verdict direction against its own why — rows 3-6 all carried Neeko-favourable whys under Skill/Veigar sides, which is exactly the 'row argues with itself' defect the chart rule describes, and the flip resolves it in the direction both the packet and the content layer already agree on. Ratings untouched. FALSE POSITIVE CONFIRMED: packet.suspectNames flags "Event Horizon's" in whys[4]; the name is correct and no edit was made. NUMERIC ERROR CORRECTED: dosFull[2].d described the cage as a 'fifteen-second invitation' — it is 20s at rank 1 and only 14s at rank 5, so the number was wrong for the entire window the advice applies to. Two genuinely absent mechanics are now on the page: Primordial Burst scaling on the target's MISSING health (which reverses the instinct to trade while low), and Phenomenal Evil stacking off spell hits on champions, not just Baleful Strike farm kills — meaning his poke on you is itself permanent scaling. The existing 'only the cage EDGE stuns' guidance was verified against Riot's text and kept; I did not add any claim about walking out through the ring, since the edge stuns on pass-through in both directions.
